economics.title: Tariffs
economics.description: Net metering means the meter physically runs backwards, so every exported kWh saves an imported one. That is temporary by nature -- the integration keeps calculating all three models side by side so you can see what a meter swap will cost.

data_description.price_per_kwh: Per kWh in your currency, e.g. 0.30 -- not in cents.
data_description.feed_in_tariff: Per kWh in your currency, e.g. 0.0786 -- not in cents.
data_description.investment_eur: Total system cost; the amortisation sensors divide it by the running savings.
data_description.commissioning_date: Start of the savings total and the amortisation clock. Empty means counting starts today.

entities.title: Plant and weather entities
entities.description: All optional. A grid power sensor enables the export-aware savings calculation; a pyranometer or illuminance sensor lets the bias model learn against measured irradiance instead of the forecast's own analysis.

data_description.grid_power_entity: Sign convention: positive = importing from the grid, negative = exporting. A reversed sign flips the savings calculation.
data_description.battery_soc_entity: Also used by battery-coupled curtailment groups to spot a full battery.

advanced.title: Model and collection
advanced.description: The watchdog only supplies support points when an entity goes quiet; event-driven updates are used as they arrive. Thirty seconds keeps ten support points in every five-minute window during an outage.

data_description.albedo: Fraction 0-1: 0.2 is grass, 0.8 is fresh snow.
data_description.system_efficiency: Fraction 0-1, e.g. 0.90 -- cable, inverter and soiling losses. Not a percentage.
data_description.retention_days: Only the 5-minute raw rows are purged; hourly aggregates and geometry history are kept.

user.title: Add PV string
user.description: Point this at the physical measurement channel, not at a min/max, template or group helper. Aggregate helpers double-count one channel and silently drop another, which is invisible in the plant total and fatal per string.

data_description.kwp: Sum of the module datasheet ratings (STC) on this input. This is DC module power -- not the inverter's AC rating.
data_description.temp_coeff: Power coefficient from the module datasheet as a fraction per Kelvin: -0.4 %/K = -0.004.
data_description.energy_entity: Cross-check only; it never feeds the forecast.
data_description.string_efficiency: Fraction between 0.5 and 1.0, e.g. 0.85. Leave at 0 to inherit the plant value.
data_description.max_power_w: Hardware cap of this single tracker input, e.g. 430 W per channel on many micro-inverters. Caps the forecast and marks measurements at the cap as censored.
data_description.charger_state_entity: A text state such as Victron's bulk/absorption/float. In absorption or float the measured power is treated as the effective limit.
data_description.mppt_output_entity: Battery-side power of this string's MPPT charge controller. With the panel power above it forms a measured pair, which lets the MPPT efficiency be learned instead of assumed. Collected only; nothing uses it yet.

user.title: Add curtailment group
user.description: Strings that can only be curtailed together -- normally one group per inverter. A commanded limit is not curtailment: it only counts once the available power actually reaches it. A permanent cap such as 800 W belongs in the fixed limit only if it caps what your string sensors measure; behind a battery it does not.

data.name: Name
data.soc_limit: State of charge at which charging stops

data_description.limit_entity: An entity reporting the currently commanded limit in percent, e.g. OpenDTU's relative limit. 100 % means the hardware maximum.
data_description.inverter_max_ac_w: The technical AC maximum from the inverter datasheet, e.g. 2400 W. NOT a legal feed-in cap such as 800 W. Only used to turn a relative limit in percent into watts.
data_description.limit_abs_entity: An entity reporting the commanded limit in watts, e.g. OpenDTU's absolute limit. Takes precedence over the relative one.
data_description.fixed_limit_w: Only for plants whose *measured* power is itself capped -- a grid-tied inverter permanently set to 800 W, with the string sensors behind that cap. Leave empty when the cap sits behind a battery: trackers measuring DC before the battery legitimately produce more, and every such interval would be censored as curtailed, which costs exactly the best observations. Applies on top of the limit entities -- the lower value wins.
data_description.battery_coupled: The inverter throttles once the battery is full. Uses the plant-level battery state of charge from the options.
data_description.soc_limit: Above this state of charge the battery counts as full, and throttled output is treated as curtailment.
data_description.output_path: What this group's DC forecast should be converted into. 'No conversion' keeps everything exactly as before.

data.name: Name
data.soc_limit: State of charge at which charging stops

data_description.limit_entity: An entity reporting the currently commanded limit in percent, e.g. OpenDTU's relative limit. 100 % means the hardware maximum.
data_description.inverter_max_ac_w: The technical AC maximum from the inverter datasheet, e.g. 2400 W. NOT a legal feed-in cap such as 800 W -- that belongs in the fixed limit below. Only used to turn a relative limit in percent into watts.
data_description.limit_abs_entity: An entity reporting the commanded limit in watts, e.g. OpenDTU's absolute limit. Takes precedence over the relative one.
data_description.fixed_limit_w: A cap configured permanently in the inverter, e.g. the legal 800 W of a balcony plant. Applies on top of the limit entities -- the lower value wins.
data_description.battery_coupled: The inverter throttles once the battery is full. Uses the plant-level battery state of charge from the options.
data_description.soc_limit: Above this state of charge the battery counts as full, and throttled output is treated as curtailment.
data_description.output_path: What this group's DC forecast should be converted into. 'No conversion' keeps everything exactly as before.

conversion.title: Conversion
conversion.description: Optional stages between the panels and what you actually get. Defaults are neutral or datasheet values; the forecast itself stays DC-based underneath.

data.forecast_clipping: Clip forecast at rated AC power

data_description.inverter_model: Datasheet efficiency curve. 'No curve' passes DC through unchanged.
data_description.custom_curve: Only for 'Custom curve': comma-separated support points, e.g. 5:0.90, 20:0.955, 50:0.967, 100:0.962. Load in percent of the AC rating, efficiency as a fraction.
data_description.forecast_clipping: Caps the AC forecast at the inverter hardware maximum. Applied to hourly means, so brief peaks inside a bright hour are understated.
data_description.ac_power_entity: The inverter's AC output sensor. Stored for the upcoming learning stage; not used yet.
data_description.mppt_efficiency: Only for charge controllers in front of the battery (e.g. Victron). 0 = no separate stage. Micro-inverters already include MPPT losses in their curve — never configure both.
data_description.charge_efficiency: DC path into the battery. The forecast ends at the battery terminal.
data_description.discharge_efficiency: Stored for plausibility checks only; discharge is a control decision, not a forecast.
data_description.curve_learning: Corrects the datasheet curve with measured DC/AC pairs. Needs the measured AC power above. Off by default: learning changes forecast numbers. The datasheet stays the starting point and the fallback.
data_description.curve_max_deviation_pp: How far a learned point may sit from the datasheet, in percentage points. The guard against one bad sensor day rewriting the curve.
data_description.curve_min_samples: Weighted five-minute pairs at which a load point is half measurement, half datasheet. Points move gradually with the evidence behind them, so there is no step where an unmeasured neighbour meets a measured one; a point nobody measured stays exactly on the datasheet.

confirm.title: Please confirm
confirm.description: Some of what you entered is usually a misconfiguration, but not always. Tick each box you have checked, or close this dialog and change the value.

data.ack_fixed_limit_with_battery: The fixed limit really does cap what the string sensors measure. On a battery-coupled plant the trackers usually measure DC before the battery, where production legitimately exceeds the limit — and every such interval would be censored as curtailed

error.nameplate_required: A relative limit in percent needs the inverter hardware maximum to be converted into watts.
error.curve_invalid: Curve needs at least two 'load:efficiency' pairs with strictly increasing load (0–150 %) and efficiency between 0.5 and 1.0.
error.nameplate_required_conversion: A curve or clipping needs the inverter hardware maximum (AC) from the previous page — load and cap both divide by it.
error.must_acknowledge: Tick this to continue, or close the dialog and change the value.

options.correction: It was wrong from the start (correct the last period)

recalculate.name: Recalculate
recalculate.description: Fetch a fresh irradiance forecast and rebuild the prediction.

reset_learning.name: Reset learning
reset_learning.description: Discard learned corrections and fall back to pure physics — for one string or the whole plant. Measurements are kept.

string_id.name: String (optional)
string_id.description: Reset only this string's observations and factors — the repair after correcting one string's geometry. Leave empty to reset everything.

purge.name: Purge raw data
purge.description: Delete raw five-minute data older than the retention period. Hourly aggregates, geometry and model state are kept.

add_geometry.name: Add geometry period
add_geometry.description: Record a new mounting geometry from a given date. Existing periods are left untouched, so historical data keeps being evaluated correctly.

config_entry_id.name: Plant
config_entry_id.description: Which plant the string belongs to.

string_id.name: String ID
string_id.description: Subentry ID of the string, as shown in the diagnostics download.

valid_from.name: Valid from
valid_from.description: Start of the new period. Defaults to now.

backfill_shading.name: Backfill shading from history
backfill_shading.description: Reconstruct shading observations from Home Assistant's long-term statistics and a historical irradiance archive. Lets the per-string shading correction start from months of real data instead of waiting a full year of seasons. Safe to run more than once.

days.name: Days of history
days.description: How far back to look. Hours without statistics are skipped.
